description: The home improvement retailer Lowe’s was founded in 1921. The brand operates 1,750 home improvement stores and employs approximately 200,000 associates. Its big-box stores, website, and app complete some 16 million customer transactions a week in the United States. Lowe’s sells DIY products, decor, tools, and gardening supplies, as well as raw materials for builders and contractors. It also sells appliances and electrical items, and offers installation services through independent contractors. Founded as a general store, Lowe’s pivoted to focusing entirely on home improvement in the 1940s, ahead of the postwar building boom, and is now the world’s second-largest home improvement retailer. It became a publicly traded company in 1961.

Employees say:

"Management and Senior Leadership communicate freely to build and earn the employees' trust daily. They involve the associates as well as all leadership when it comes to ideas and thoughts on improving and making changes. This gives those involved ownership and pride when a part of the team. The Managers and Senior Leadership are willing to help and jump in when needed and not just sit back and watch."

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The home improvement retailer reported revenue of $97.1 billion in fiscal 2022, a roughly 1% increase from the prior year, as the COVID-era boom in home repairs eased.

  • Overall transactions at the company declined 7.4% in 2022 compared with the year prior, another sign of the slowdown in home improvement projects.

  • In July 2022 Lowe’s adopted a four-day workweek for full-time store staff. Frontline employees had complained for years that Lowe’s old scheduling system was unpredictable and afforded few consecutive days off.

  • In February 2023 Lowe’s completed the sale of its 450-store Canadian business to private equity firm Sycamore Partners for $400 million.

  • Lowe’s is led by Marvin Ellison, one of only eight Black CEOs in the Fortune 500.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: The big-box home-improvement retailer has enjoyed several strong years, as the pandemic and the rise of remote work encouraged many people to either update their existing homes or buy and fix up new ones. The company reported more than $96 billion in sales in 2021, a bump of 6.9% compared with 2020, and an impressive 33% leap from 2019, the last pre-pandemic year. A tight housing market and rising real estate values are expected to continue to fuel new home projects—good news for Lowe’s and its competitors.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Housebound Americans lavished billions on their homes last year at stores such as Lowe’s, setting up home offices and getting around to the small projects they suddenly had ample time for. Lowe’s sales rose 24.2% to just under $90 billion on that macro tailwind, narrowing its performance gap with rival Home Depot. The home improvement giant also helped itself with a vastly improved e-commerce site and savvy merchandising moves, such as stocking a wider assortment of holiday season goods like exercise bikes. While the home spending boom could ease this year, Lowe’s is redoubling its efforts to win more business from contractors who do larger projects.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Lowe’s has played second fiddle to Home Depot for years now, lagging its bigger rival by sales growth and e-commerce prowess. But Lowe’s is making big strides with its store brands, and it has made major technical changes to rev up its e-commerce site. Additionally, the company's big appliance business is booming. The economic downturn is likely to cool a housing market that has allowed Lowe’s to thrive despite some weaknesses, which include meager online growth. But it seems, for now, Lowe’s has begun to address those competitive disadvantages.
